# 2nd Kalasha International Film & TV Awards

The 2nd Kalasha Film and Television Awards ceremony, presented by the Kenya Film Commission, honoured the best in Kenyan television and film for the year 2010. The event took place on 25 September 2010 at the KICC in Nairobi, Kenya. The awards celebrate cultural diversity through film and aim to motivate local producers towards high-quality film and television productions.
Nick Reding's Ndoto za Elibidi and Hawa Essuman's Soul Boy (shot entirely in Kibera) were the major winners in the film categories. Ndoto za Elibidi won Best Feature Film, Best Editingand Best Supporting Actress, while Soul Boy secured Best Short Film, Best Lead Actorand Best Scriptwriter. In television, the hit show Papa Shirandula dominated the comedy categories, with the late Charles Bukeko winning Best Actor in a TV Series.
Ceremony
The 2nd edition of the awards ceremony was a glamorous gala night at the KICC, Nairobi, Kenya, featuring a red carpet, limousinesand attendees mostly clad in African apparel. The event was hosted by media personalities Caroline Mutuko and Eddie Kimani, with musical performances by gospel sensation Emmy Kosgei, Carol Atemiand Linda Muthama.
The ceremony was graced by prominent political figures who attended in African attire to endorse and support the continuity of local storytelling. Guests of honour included the then Minister of Finance Uhuru Kenyatta, Minister of Information and Communication Samuel Poghisio alongside his Permanent Secretary Bitange Ndemo, Minister of Medical Services Anyang' Nyong'oand P. L. O. Lumumba. Minister Kenyatta praised local broadcasters for their support and highlighted the film industry's potential to provide employment for Kenyan youth.
Broadcaster Royal Media Services (Citizen TV) and the Kenya Institute of Mass Communication (KIMC) reigned supreme during the night, bagging multiple awards in their respective categories.
